The exact closed model facts confirm no DoorShut-to-DoorShut edge exists in the complete 33-transition inventory. The PlantUML source shows 'DoorShut : Cancel' as a description note, not a transition declaration, so the source itself fails to encode the required behavior. The strongest alternative reading—that the compiler faithfully transcribed the source—is defeated because the NL is the normative contract, not the source; fidelity to a defective source does not satisfy the NL obligation. No competent defeater survives.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0005:r1:i2: NL-CONTRACT-REF-014 (NL6) requirement quote 'canceling or updating the cooking time'; FCSTM transition:line:40 effects=["R45RouteToken = 0"]; reference_inspection_facts variables count=1 (R45RouteToken only); closed model inventory confirms no cooking-time variable.
decisions.reason: NL6 requires a semantic effect of 'canceling or updating the cooking time' on the ReadytoCook→DoorShutWithItem Cancel transition. The exact binding identifies transition:line:40 as the carrier. The closed model inventory shows effects=["R45RouteToken = 0"] on that transition and declares only one variable (R45RouteToken), with no cooking-time variable present. The rebutting reading—that R45RouteToken=0 proxies a cooking-time reset—is defeated by the exact model fact that R45RouteToken is a compiler-internal routing token and no cooking-time variable exists in the model. The violation is semantically established: the required effect is absent.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The R45RouteToken=0 effect on transition:line:40 could be interpreted as resetting a cooking-time variable, satisfying the cancel/update requirement implicitly.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition from ReadytoCook to DoorShutWithItem on Cancel must carry an effect that cancels or updates the cooking time, per NL6.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0005:r1:i4: NL-CONTRACT-REF-019 (NL8) requirement quote 'opening the door stops the timer'; FCSTM transition:line:24 effects=["R45RouteToken = 17"]; segments transition:line:29/42/55 have no effects; reference_inspection_facts variables count=1 (R45RouteToken only); no timer variable in model.
decisions.reason: NL8 requires a semantic effect of 'opening the door stops the timer' on the Cooking→DoorOpenWithItem door-opened transition. The exact binding identifies transition:line:24 as the trigger-consumption segment (ActiveCooking→[*], Open_Door, effect R45RouteToken=17). Subsequent routing segments (transition:line:29, 42, 55) carry no effects. The closed model declares only R45RouteToken as a variable; no timer variable or explicit stop action exists. The rebutting reading—that exiting Cooking implicitly stops an external timer—is defeated because the NL explicitly frames 'stops the timer' as a behavioral effect that should be represented in the model, and no such data manipulation or action is present in any segment of macro tr_0017. The violation is semantically established.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The R45RouteToken=17 effect on transition:line:24 initiates routing that eventually exits Cooking, implicitly stopping the timer by leaving the active-cooking state.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition from Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem on door opened must carry an effect that stops the timer, per NL8.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0005:r1:i5: NL-CONTRACT-REF-019 (NL8) requirement quote 'opening the door stops the timer'; FCSTM macro tr_0017 segments transition:line:24/29/42/55 with no timer-stop effect in any; states Cooking:line:21 and DoorOpenWithItem:line:13 confirm endpoint relation; reference_inspection_facts variables count=1 (R45RouteToken only).
decisions.reason: NL8 states 'opening the door stops the timer' as a behavioral effect. The candidate examines the entire macro tr_0017 across all four segments: transition:line:24 (effect R45RouteToken=17), transition:line:29 (effects=[]), transition:line:42 (effects=[]), transition:line:55 (effect R45RouteToken=0). No segment carries a timer-stop effect. The model declares no timer variable (only R45RouteToken). The endpoint relation (Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem) is satisfied, so this is not a reachability or endpoint issue—it is specifically the absence of the required semantic effect. The external-hardware-timer rebuttal is defeated because the NL frames the stop as a behavioral effect the model should represent, and the exact model inventory confirms no such representation exists. The violation is established across the full macro scope.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The timer could be an external hardware timer implicitly stopped by the state transition leaving Cooking/ActiveCooking, making an explicit model-level effect unnecessary.
decisions.violated_obligation: The macro tr_0017 representing Cooking-to-DoorOpenWithItem on door opened must carry a semantic effect of stopping the timer in at least one segment, per NL8.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0005:r1:i6: source 0005.puml:line:4 text 'DoorShut : Cancel' (PlantUML description syntax); model state:DoorShut:line:50 has no action or self-transition for Cancel; event:Cancel:line:10 exists but is not bound to DoorShut; closed model inventory confirms absence of Cancel action/transition on DoorShut.
decisions.reason: The NL contract (derived from 0005.puml:line:4) requires that Cancel be either an action of DoorShut or a trigger labeling a transition on DoorShut. The exact source fact shows line 4 is `DoorShut : Cancel`, which in PlantUML state diagram syntax is a description string, not an executable action (actions require entry:/exit:/do: prefixes or transition labeling). The closed model inventory confirms no action or self-transition labeled Cancel exists on state:DoorShut:line:50. The event:Cancel:line:10 exists in the model but is not connected to DoorShut by any transition or action. No competent alternative reading satisfies the NL property: the text is semantically inert as a description. The violation is established—Cancel has no executable effect on DoorShut.
decisions.violated_obligation: If DoorShut must remain in DoorShut upon Cancel, the model must have an action or self-transition labeled Cancel on DoorShut; per the NL, the system can remain in DoorShut if a Cancel action is performed.

The subsequent routing segments (transition:line:29, transition:line:42, transition:line:55) carry no effects. No timer-stop effect exists anywhere in the macro tr_0017.
issues.reason: The NL8 contract requires a semantic effect (stop timer) on the Cooking→DoorOpenWithItem door-opened transition. The frozen predicate registry has no effect predicate, so this remains predicate-null W1. The carrier is the trigger-consumption segment transition:line:24 where Open_Door is received.
issues.requirement_quote: opening the door stops the timer
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The R45RouteToken=17 effect initiates routing that eventually exits Cooking, which implicitly stops the timer by leaving the state; however, no explicit timer-stop action or variable assignment is declared.
issues.title: Missing effect on Cooking→DoorOpenWithItem door-opened transition: stop timer

issues.basis: NL8 text; FCSTM macro tr_0017 segments (transition:line:24, 29, 42, 55); none carry a timer-stop effect; reference_inspection_facts variables count=1 (R45RouteToken only); no timer variable or action in model text.
issues.expected: The transition from Cooking to DoorOpenWithItem on door opened must carry the semantic effect of stopping the timer.
issues.observed: The macro tr_0017 spans 4 FCSTM segments: transition:line:24 (ActiveCooking→[*], Open_Door, effect R45RouteToken=17), transition:line:29 (Cooking→[*], guard R45RouteToken==17, effects=[]), transition:line:42 (ReadytoCook→[*], guard R45RouteToken==17, effects=[]), transition:line:55 (DoorOpenWithItem→DoorOpenWithItem, guard R45RouteToken==17, effects=[R45RouteToken=0]). No segment carries a 'stop timer' effect. No timer variable exists in the model.
issues.reason: The contract requires a specific semantic effect ('stop timer') on the Cooking→DoorOpenWithItem door-opened transition. The macro exists and the endpoint relation is satisfied, but no segment in the macro carries the required timer-stop effect. No timer variable exists. The frozen predicate registry has no effect-checking predicate, so this remains predicate-null.
issues.requirement_quote: opening the door stops the timer
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The timer could be interpreted as an external hardware timer that is implicitly stopped by the state transition (leaving Cooking/ActiveCooking). However, the NL explicitly states 'opening the door stops the timer' as a behavioral effect, and no such data manipulation or action is present in the model.
